intervals.quote: The R&D project COSINUS (Cryogenic Observatory for SIgnatures seen in Next-generation Underground Searches) aims to develop a cryogenic scintillating calorimeter using NaI as target crystal for direct darkmatter search.

leadership.note: Affiliation on the page: Marietta-Blau-Institut fuer Teilchenphysik, TU Wien. Term dates are not published.

website.quote: Cryogenic calorimeters for dark matter search using NaI scintillating crystals at Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso, Italy

name: COSINUS Collaboration
notes: Roster not recorded: the home page gives 'over 40 scientists' only; the Atlas records no memberships.

Project partners per the MPP page: 'The project is led by a team from the Max Planck Institute for Physics, HEPHY, TU Wien, and INFN and GSSI (Italy). Other actors include SICCAS (China) and the Helsinki Institute for Physics (Finland).'

summary.plain: The international team building COSINUS, a dark matter detector at the Gran Sasso laboratory that uses cold sodium iodide crystals to test the yearly signal reported by DAMA/LIBRA. Its home page says a team of over 40 scientists, engineers, postdocs and students works on it.
summary.technical: COSINUS (Cryogenic Observatory for SIgnatures seen in Next-generation Underground Searches): led from TU Wien (spokesperson Florian Reindl) and the Max Planck Institute for Physics, with HEPHY Vienna, INFN and GSSI (Italy), the Helsinki Institute of Physics and SICCAS (China) named on the MPP project page; authors of the 2024 prototype papers are listed as 'COSINUS Collaboration'.
